On iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.3 with Archie 0.3.9 on the computer; the Android download does not have it yet. Your computer sends them, so it has to be on, awake and running Archie. Its window can be closed. Only the owner's phone gets them. A teammate's phone does not. On an agent with a chat app connected, a reply's notification comes about 15 seconds after your agent goes quiet. What each one says is locked on your computer and opened on your phone, so we, Apple and Google pass it along without reading it.

entries.t: A phone message waits for a sleeping computer
entries.s: A message sent from Archie Mobile while your computer sleeps waits and says so, and your agent answers it when the computer wakes, knowing it was sent earlier.
entries.x: In Archie Mobile, on the waiting message. To take back a waiting message, press Remove it. In Archie Mobile on iPhone and Android. Your agent answers only once the computer running Archie is on and Archie is open. Remove it works only if the computer has not picked the message up yet. Nobody has yet tried it on a real phone against a sleeping computer.

entries.t: Run a routine or tune a skill from your phone
entries.s: From Archie Mobile you can run a routine now, pick a skill's Response quality, and switch a skill's scheduled messages off and on.
entries.x: In Archie Mobile, on a skill's or routine's row, which opens in place. In Archie Mobile, open your agent's skills or routines. Press a row to open it, then press Run now or change a setting. In Archie Mobile on iPhone and Android. The computer running Archie does the work, so it has to be on, awake and running Archie. Connecting an account for a skill still happens at the computer. Nobody has watched it on a real phone yet.

entries.s: When you type your brokerage, phone number, or business name into a blank on an email draft, the card offers Keep for every draft.
entries.x: On an email draft card, after you fill in a blank with Edit it. Press Edit it on the draft and fill in the blank. Press Keep for every draft. Archie Mobile shows the card's words and buttons. A chat app with no buttons takes the typed words. Email cards only. Text drafts are never filled. If you changed the words around the blank too, no button appears. Only on your own email address.

entries.s: The first time your agent checks your mail, it says in the chat which inboxes it reads and how often, with a Stop watching button.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. The switch it turns off is Watch my inbox, on the agent's Skills tab, under Email Manager. Press Stop watching under the message, or switch off Watch my inbox under Email Manager on the Skills tab. It arrives in your conversation like any message, so it also shows on Archie Mobile or your chat app. It says so once per agent. Switching the watch off and on again does not repeat it. Only the owner can stop it from the button. Not on the free credits or a plan with the AI included, where your mail is not read.

entries.t: Mail from people you write to comes first
entries.s: Mail from someone you wrote to in the last two weeks is read at once; other mail can wait a few minutes, which lowers what your AI account is charged.
entries.x: It knows one thing: whether you wrote to the sender in the last 14 days. Replies from Archie's cards count on any account, and Gmail's Sent copies count. A reply sent from Outlook or another mail app is not seen. The addresses you wrote to are kept on your computer and in backups you make. Only on an AI account of your own with Anthropic.

entries.s: Your agent leaves a blank in square brackets, like [her school], for a detail nobody gave, and an email or text with a blank in it will not send.
entries.x: On an email or text card. Press Send and Archie names the blank. Edit it is on the card. Press Edit it on the card. Fill in what goes in the brackets. Press Send. Archie Mobile's Send gives the same answer and puts the buttons back. On a chat app with no buttons, reply "edit it". Leaving a blank is an instruction to the AI, and it can still write a guess as if it were known. Any short words in brackets count, so a [sic] holds Send too. Brackets in your current signature do not. On a card waiting for its time, press Back to draft first, then Edit it. A message written into the chat for you to copy, or one through a connected CRM, is not checked.

entries.s: On an email your agent drafts in chat, a price, a day, or a time that nobody gave it is listed under the draft for you to check.
entries.x: Under the draft on an email card. Archie Mobile shows the card's own words, the list included. Only amounts, days, and times are read for this. A reason or a promise is listed only when your agent names it. It lists them. It does not stop Send. Not on texts, and not on drafts the mail watch writes when mail arrives. A number that appears anywhere in what you gave counts as given, and editing the card's words clears the list.

entries.s: Ask your agent to text a lead, and it writes the text, says whether they agreed to texts, and puts a button under it so you can send it yourself.
entries.x: Under your agent's reply in Chat: Copy the text. Ask your agent to text a lead by name. Press Copy the text, or Open in Messages on your phone. Press Send in Messages yourself. Archie Mobile shows Open in Messages, which opens Messages to their number with the words typed in. A chat app gets the words and no button. Archie sends no text. You press Send on your own phone. It reads what the Texting column says, which someone wrote down. It does not enforce consent. Only where a list keeps a Texting column, which today is the real estate setup's People. If they said stop, it writes no text.

entries.t: Ask what's on, what's due, or what's free
entries.s: Ask about some days and Archie hands your agent what your lists, your calendar, and your reminders hold for those days before it answers.
entries.x: Ask your agent a question that names a day and the schedule, such as "What's on Saturday?" or "What's due this week?" Your agent answers from your lists, your calendar, and your reminders, and says where each thing came from. A question typed on a chat app or in Archie Mobile gets the same kind of answer, because the computer running Archie gathers it. It goes by the words of a question you type. "Am I around Friday?" has no schedule word, and routines and the mail and text watches never get it. What is free works only on lists shaped like the restroom trailer and portable restroom setups, and it goes by the day, never the hour. It reads what is written on your lists and one calendar on each connected account. A booking that is only in an email or a text is left out. What it finds for those days goes to your AI company with your question.

entries.t: Dates from your lists on the Calendar
entries.s: The Calendar tab shows the dates on your lists beside your calendar events, reminders, and routines, so a booking kept on a list shows on its day.
entries.x: On your agent's Calendar tab, marked On your lists in the legend. Press a date's title and that list opens. Open your agent's Calendar tab. Look for the dates marked On your lists, at the head of each day. Press one to open its list. In Archie Mobile, the Calendar under More shows the same dates for the next seven days, and pressing one opens Lists rather than that one list. Pressing a list date opens the list and changes nothing. Which dates count is read off the column names, so a list whose names are misread can show an old date or hide a coming one. Birthdays and anniversaries come round every year. The computer shows a week at a time. The phone shows the next seven days and does not move.

entries.t: Your to-do list on the Dashboard
entries.s: Your to-do list is the first thing on your agent's Dashboard, where you can tick something off or add one without asking your agent.
entries.x: On the agent's Dashboard tab, the first card, with Add a to-do at the bottom. Open your agent's Dashboard. Tick a to-do to mark it done, or type one in Add a to-do. Archie Mobile shows the same list first on the Dashboard, where you can tick to-dos off and add new ones. Only on an agent with the Task Manager add-on. To-dos kept in Todoist or Google Tasks do not show here. Something waiting on you, like a draft to send, sits above it. A checklist your agent already posted in the chat updates only when your agent next touches the list. Change a date or a priority by telling your agent, or in the list on the Knowledge tab.

entries.s: A list can show its steps, like Quoted, Booked, Out and Picked up, with each entry's step in color and a count at each step.
entries.x: On the Knowledge tab, under Lists, under Stages on the list's own form. Open the list on the Knowledge tab, under Lists. Under Stages, pick the choice column that holds the steps. Or ask your agent to turn a list's steps on. Archie Mobile shows the count at each step under Lists, in the same colors, and on iPhone opens a list's entries to add or change them. Nothing enforces the steps. An entry can skip one, and moving an entry starts nothing by itself.

entries.t: Lists in the sidebar and on the Dashboard
entries.s: Keep up to six lists in your agent's sidebar, under Jobs, and each one shows on the Dashboard with its count and where its entries stand.
entries.x: On the list, press Keep in the sidebar. Kept lists show in the sidebar after Jobs and as tiles on the Dashboard. Open a list on the Knowledge tab, under Lists. Press Keep in the sidebar. Archie Mobile lists the kept lists after Jobs on More. Up to six lists. On Archie for Teams, keeping a shared list in one agent's sidebar puts it in nobody else's.

entries.t: Lists made from what you tell your agent
entries.s: When you first set up your agent and say what work you do, it drafts up to three lists that work runs on, with their steps.
entries.x: Answer your agent's first questions about your work. It drafts lists only from what you said, and only when your work comes in rows. It happens at the first questions. An agent set up earlier does not get lists by itself. On the free credits and the plan with the AI included, nobody has yet seen it work on a real account.

entries.s: The last of your agent's first questions is where you keep your work today, and its goodbye offers one way to bring that in.
entries.x: Under the goodbye in your agent's chat: Add the spreadsheet, Add the exported file, Add a photo of a page, Connect my calendar, or Connect Follow Up Boss. Answer where you keep your work. Press the button under the goodbye and pick the file or photo. Press Send, then press Add on the card when the entries look right. In Archie Mobile, the file and photo buttons open the phone's file picker or camera. There is no calendar button there, and chat apps show no button. It opens a picker. You choose and send the file, and nothing is added until you press a button on its card. In your head, somewhere else, or a skipped answer gets no button, except a realtor's Tell me your open deals. Other software means an exported file, unless you named Follow Up Boss. The AI words the question and reads your answer, so a roundabout answer can be misread.

entries.t: Bring in a spreadsheet someone emailed
entries.s: Say "bring in the spreadsheet Dana emailed", and your agent finds the email, opens the file, and puts its rows on a card for you to add.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. When your work is in a spreadsheet, the goodbye of the first questions also has Someone else has it. Ask your agent to bring in the spreadsheet somebody emailed you. Look over the rows on the card, then press its button to add them. Ask from Archie Mobile the same way, or press + and then Choose a file to send one yourself. Only on an AI account of your own with your mail connected. Otherwise, Archie says how to save the file and send it in the chat. Nothing reaches the other person, and nothing is added until you press a button. It has not opened a file from a real mailbox yet.

entries.s: Ask who owes you money, and your agent answers from entries on your lists marked billed and not paid, oldest first, with the days each has waited.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. Ask "Who owes me money?", "Who hasn't been billed yet?", or "Who still owes a deposit?" Ask from Archie Mobile or a chat app, and the answer arrives like any reply. It reads your own lists. It does not connect to QuickBooks or any accounting app. It knows what was written down: an entry counts as owed because its billing says Billed. A deposit is a step on a booking. Nothing records the money arriving. It answers this way only when the question uses words like owe, unpaid, overdue, or invoice.

entries.t: Fixing a save your agent claimed but never made
entries.s: If a reply says it put something on your lists and nothing was saved, Archie adds a line saying so, with Save it to save it now.
entries.x: Under your agent's reply in Chat. Press Save it, or reply "save it" where there is no button. The line is part of the reply, and Archie Mobile, Telegram, Slack, and Discord show Save it. It catches certain words in a sentence about a list. A claim worded another way passes. Only claims about lists are corrected. "I've updated your calendar" or a note about you gets no line. No Save it button on Signal, iMessage, or Matrix. Save it is a request: your agent saves on that turn, with the usual Undo.

entries.t: A new list takes its first entries
entries.s: Ask for a new list and say what goes on it in the same message, and your agent makes the list and adds those entries in one reply.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. Ask for the list and name its first entries in one message. It works the same from Archie Mobile or a chat app. Making a list is for the owner, or a teammate allowed to act as the owner. This is about an agent's first list. An agent that already has a list could always add entries at once.

entries.s: Ask your agent who to call, and Archie works it out from your People and Deals lists: birthdays, closing anniversaries, quiet leads, and past clients.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. Ask "Who should I call this week?" or "Which leads have gone quiet?" Ask from Archie Mobile or a chat app, and the answer arrives like any reply. Only lists called People, Deals, Your leads, and Listings are read, which the real estate setup and Lead Desk make. It knows what was written down. An empty Last contact means nobody wrote one, even if you did talk. Only an email reply sent through Archie updates Last contact. Texts, calls, and other mail do not. Someone marked Said stop is listed as call or email only. Nothing blocks a text to them.

entries.s: When your agent adds someone, Archie looks on your lists for the same phone number, email, or name, and your agent says who it may be.
entries.x: In your agent's chat, after it adds an entry. It works the same from Archie Mobile or a chat app. It adds first and asks after. Nothing is merged or refused. Only entries your agent adds one at a time are checked, not ones from the Lists screen, an import, or a card. A shared last name is enough only when one of the two has no phone and no email.

entries.t: Hear when a booking puts something in two places
entries.s: When a booking puts a trailer or a unit in two places on the same day, Archie saves it as asked and says which booking it runs into.
entries.x: On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists, the note after Added or Saved says it. A card's Add and the chat's import card say it too. Nothing stops the booking. It is saved as you asked or typed it, and you decide which one changes. Only lists shaped like the two rental setups are checked, by the day and never the hour. A tech sent to two jobs at once is not caught. When your agent saves the booking itself, you hear about it only if its reply says so. More than 200 entries added at once are not checked, and the note says to look over the busy days on the Calendar tab instead.

entries.t: Bring a spreadsheet into a list
entries.s: Import a spreadsheet into one of your lists. Archie matches the columns, leaves out rows already there, and names every cell it could not read.
entries.x: On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists, open a list and press Import beside Add row. An empty list also says Have a spreadsheet of these already? Import it. Open the list on your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists. Press Import and pick the file. Under Match your columns, give each column of the file a place on the list, Leave it out, or Add it as a new column. Read what will be added and what will be left out, then press Add. To take it all back, press Undo, here or on the job on the Jobs tab. It is a copy taken once. Later changes to the file never reach the list, and changes to the list never reach the file. It adds and never updates. A row that repeats an entry is left out and never used to change it. The first sheet only, up to 5,000 rows and 20 MB. A Google Sheet has to be downloaded as a file first, and a Numbers file saved as Excel or CSV. Dates are read month first, so 3/10/2026 meant as October 3 comes in as March 10.

entries.t: Drop a spreadsheet in the chat
entries.s: Drop a spreadsheet into the chat and Archie puts up a card that names the list it fits and how many rows would come in.
entries.x: In the chat with your agent, in Archie or on a chat app that shows buttons. Drop a spreadsheet into the chat, with or without a few words. On the card, press Add, choose A different list, press Make a new list from it, or press Just keep the file. Look the rows over on the card that comes up below, change or uncheck any, then press Add. On Telegram, Slack or Discord, a spreadsheet you send gets the same card with its buttons. Words that do more than hand the file over start an ordinary reply too, and your agent may open the file, which sends what it reads to your AI company. Columns are matched by name only. The card names any column the list has no place for, and Make a new list keeps them all. The first sheet only, up to 5,000 rows and 10 MB. Sent through a chat app, the file passes through that app's servers on its way.

entries.t: Check new entries on one card before Add
entries.s: Hand your agent a photo, a page, or your calendar, and every entry it finds for one of your lists goes on one card you check before anything is added.
entries.x: On the card in the chat with your agent. It also waits on the Jobs tab, in the Needs you column, with Approve and No thanks. Send a photo or a page, paste a list, or ask your agent to go through your calendar for one of your lists. On the card, uncheck any entry to leave it off, or press Change to fix one. Press Add, or tell your agent yes. Pressing Not now leaves them all off. Undo on the card takes the whole card back off the list. The entries are what the AI read, which can be wrong. The card is there so you check them. Only entries on the card are held back. One more entry you tell your agent while it waits goes in at once. Add needs the agent running. A card waits two weeks at most and goes away with New chat. Reading a photo sends it to the AI company that reads pictures for your agent.

entries.t: Bring a shared Google Sheet into a list
entries.s: Ask your agent to bring a Google Sheet you shared with it into one of your lists. The rows come in on a card you check first.
entries.x: Share the Sheet on your agent's Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files, in Google's own file picker. On your agent's Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files, pick the Sheet in Google's file picker. Ask your agent to bring that sheet into one of your lists. Check the card, then press Add or say yes. It is a copy taken when you ask. Nothing is written to the sheet, and the two are never kept in step. Only a Sheet you picked, one tab at a time, up to 5,000 rows. Columns are matched by their names, and the card cannot change the match. It has not yet been run against a live Google account.

entries.t: How far along a list is
entries.s: Tell Archie about how many a list will hold, and it shows how many are entered so far, such as 25 of about 300 units entered.
entries.x: On the list's page, press the pencil to edit the list and fill in About how many in all, once everything is entered. Or tell your agent in the chat. Open the list on your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists. Press the pencil to edit the list. Fill in About how many in all, and save. Or tell your agent, for example "We run about 300 units." Archie Mobile's list tiles show the same count. The number is yours. Nothing counts your units anywhere but the list. It is read from your words, so "three hundred units" spelled out is missed. The list's form shows the number and changes it.

entries.t: Fold a row listed twice into one
entries.s: When a unit number or another value meant to be on a list once shows up twice, the list says so, and Review keeps the row you pick.
entries.x: On the list's page, in the line Listed more than once under the column's name, with Review. Open the list on your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists. Press Review on the Listed more than once line. Press Keep this one on the row to keep. To put both rows back, press Undo on that job on the Jobs tab. It happens only when you press it, and only in Archie on the computer. Where both rows have a value, the kept row's wins. Only long notes are joined. It finds a repeat only under a column meant to hold each value once, such as Unit number.

entries.t: Ask about a unit by number
entries.s: Ask about unit 31 and your agent finds the row titled S-31, matching names like Trailer 4 or INV-1042 by their letters and numbers.
entries.x: It only helps your agent find the row. Nothing stops it changing the wrong one. It works on rows whose titles read like a code: three words at most, ending in a number. A date, a time or an amount never counts.

entries.s: A reminder you ask for also goes on your to-do list; tick it off and the reminder is not said, and deleting it in one place removes both.
entries.x: On the Dashboard's to-do list, on the Calendar, and on the reminder's card in the chat. Ask your agent to remind you of something. To drop it, press Delete under the reply that set it, on the Dashboard, on the Calendar, or on the card when it goes off. In Archie Mobile on iPhone, swipe left on the to-do list or press Delete on the Calendar. Only on an agent with the Task Manager add-on. Promises caught from texts show on the list only with Commitment Keeper as well. Nobody has watched it in the Archie window yet.

entries.s: When a reminder goes off, Remind me later offers in an hour, this evening or tomorrow, each with its time on the button, or another time in your words.
entries.x: On the reminder's card in the chat. When a reminder goes off, press Remind me later. Pick In an hour, This evening, Tomorrow or Another time, or press Back. Nobody has watched it in the Archie window yet.

entries.t: Your agent works while you are away
entries.s: Your agent runs routines, reads new mail, and reports to you with nobody watching, for as many hours as your computer is on and Archie is open.
entries.x: Routine reports and replies reach your chat app or Archie Mobile while the computer running Archie is on. Your computer has to be on with Archie open. While it is off, your agent answers nothing. Archie has no working-hours setting. The hours are whenever your computer is on and Archie is open. A routine can wake a sleeping computer. A computer that is shut down stays off. Mail that arrived while the computer was off is read when it is back on, within a limit.

entries.s: For a line of work Archie has a setup for, your agent can send what is on today each morning, built from your lists without asking an AI.
entries.x: On the Routines tab, the Morning list row has its switch. Your agent also offers it at the end of your first evening. Say yes when your agent offers it at the end of your first evening, or switch on Morning list on the Routines tab. Or say "send me the morning list" in the chat. Press Another time under the offer to pick a time before noon, or say "send me the morning list at 6:30am". To stop it, press Stop on the list, or say "stop the morning list". It arrives in your chat with your agent, and Archie Mobile's Routines screen has the same Morning list switch. Only for the lines of work Archie has a setup for: portable restrooms, home trades, event trailers and real estate. It comes only after you say yes, and only on mornings with something on it. It needs Archie running and your computer awake at some point between its time and noon. A computer asleep until after noon gets none that day. It goes only to your own chat with your agent. Your team does not see it.

entries.t: Waking the computer for a routine
entries.s: A routine set for seven in the morning arrives at seven, even if your computer was asleep. Archie wakes it a few minutes before, runs it, and lets it sleep.
entries.x: On the Routines tab, a routine that missed a run while your computer slept shows Wake this computer. Press it, then Set this up. On the Routines tab, open a routine that missed a run while your computer slept. Press Wake this computer, then Set this up. On a Mac, type your password in macOS's own box. Archie never sees what you type. On Windows it is one press, with nothing to approve. It wakes a sleeping computer. One that is shut down stays off, so choose Sleep instead of Shut Down. On a Mac, setting it up asks for an administrator's password once. On Windows, the power plan has to allow wake timers. If it does not, the routine shows the steps to change it. Only a routine set for a time of day wakes your computer. One that runs every few minutes does not.

entries.t: Missed routines run when the computer wakes
entries.s: A routine due while your computer was asleep runs when it wakes, as long as that is the same morning, afternoon, or evening. Past that, its row says it missed.
entries.x: The line under the Routines tab's title says this, and a routine that missed a run says so on its row. Past noon for a morning, 6:00 PM for an afternoon, or midnight for an evening, the run is recorded as missed and not run. After your computer sleeps through several of a day's times, the routine runs the latest one, once. Routines run from the computer running Archie. A computer that is shut down runs nothing.

entries.t: One routine at several times a day
entries.s: A routine can run at several set times a day, up to 24, like 9:00 in the morning and 5:00 in the afternoon.
entries.x: On the Routines tab, open a routine and press Add a time. You can also set the times in the chat. Open the routine on the Routines tab. Press Add a time and pick the time. Or tell your agent in the chat, like "run it at 9:00am and 5:00pm". Archie Mobile shows every time a routine runs at and can move any one of them. Up to 24 set times a day. More often than that is an interval, like every 30 minutes, which counts from when it starts. Each time it runs counts as a job. On the free tier, at most 15 of a routine's runs happen in a day. After your computer sleeps through several of a day's times, it runs the latest one, once.

entries.s: Tell your agent to remind you at a time, and it does, in your own words, at that minute, without asking an AI anything to read it back.
entries.x: In the chat. Reminders also show on the Jobs tab and the Calendar tab, and on the to-do list on an agent with the To-Do List. Say "remind me at 3pm to call the dentist". When it goes off, press Done, Remind me later, or Delete. To cancel early, press Delete under the reply that set it. Archie Mobile notifies you once notifications are on in its Settings, and a chat app shows the buttons where it can draw them. Otherwise a reminder waits in the chat until you open it. One reminder is one moment. Something every week is a routine. Quiet hours do not hold a reminder back, since you named the minute. One whose minute passed while your computer slept arrives when it wakes, saying when it was for. Past a week it is dropped.

entries.t: A reminder that stands down when the person writes back
entries.s: Make a reminder conditional, like "remind me Thursday to chase the quote unless Ellen has replied". If Ellen emails or texts in first, it is dropped and Archie tells you.
entries.x: In the chat. The condition shows beside the reminder on the Jobs tab and in the list. Add "unless Ellen has replied" to a reminder you ask for, naming the person. It notices only that Ellen wrote. A note from her about something else also drops the reminder. It needs a mailbox connected or the Mac text watch. With neither, the reminder simply arrives at its time, and your agent says so. A name matches as a whole word, and an address matches exactly.

entries.s: When your agent posts on its own, like a reminder or a routine's report, your computer shows an alert with the agent's name and the first line.
entries.x: Settings, General, Show alerts on this computer. It is on from the start. To turn it off, open Settings, then General, and switch off Show alerts on this computer. This alert is on your computer only. Archie Mobile has its own notifications, once you turn them on in its Settings. It shows only while Archie is open behind your other windows, on a computer that is on and awake. Clicking the alert does not open the conversation. Archie cannot tell whether your computer blocks its alerts, so the Settings row says where your computer's own switch is. A reminder within 60 seconds of a conversation ending, on an agent with a chat app, raises no alert.

entries.s: The Knowledge tab opens like folders: Documents your agent reads, Lists it keeps up to date, Memory, and How you write.
entries.x: On the agent's Knowledge tab. Archie Mobile groups documents by the same folders. Documents are files your agent reads and never changes.

entries.s: When you first open Archie, your agent asks a few questions about your work, starting with the first thing you say, so it can help you better.
entries.x: On the first run, in the agent's chat: the card Let me tell you what I do (on Archie for Teams, Let me tell you about the business and my team), and Stop the questions. Press Let me tell you what I do, or just type. Answer its questions. If your first message asks for something, your agent does that first. Press Stop the questions to end them early. The first run happens on the computer. On a chat app, the questions start when you claim your agent. Whether your first message asks for something is the AI's judgment, so it can miss. Asking again gets it done. Your answers go to your AI company like any message. It stops after 12 messages, a second job, a question of yours, or Stop the questions, and keeps what was said by then. On the free tier its own turns are not counted, but a job asked for in your first message is one of the day's 20.

entries.s: At the top of an agent's Knowledge tab, Archie counts its lists, documents, and things it remembers about you, and shows the latest list changes with Undo.
entries.x: At the top of the agent's Knowledge tab, headed with the agent's name, such as What Ember keeps. Open the agent's Knowledge tab. Under Saved lately, press Open or Undo beside a change. Archie Mobile's Documents screen opens with the same three counts, without Saved lately. Saved lately shows list changes only: the five newest not yet taken back. Entries added from a card or an import are not in it. Undo those on the Jobs tab. Undo after forgetting a memory line puts it back as a new line, dated this month.

entries.t: What your agent remembers about you
entries.s: Your agent keeps a short list of what it has learned about you. You can read every line, add one, change one, or delete one.
entries.x: On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Memory. Each line has a pencil, Change this, and a cross, Forget this, and Clear all is at the bottom. Open your agent's Knowledge tab and choose Memory. Press the pencil beside a line to change it, or the cross to forget it. Type in the box to add a line yourself. On the owner's phone, Archie Mobile shows the same Memory under More, then Documents, while the computer running Archie is on. It carries only what has come up lately. Older lines go to a file it looks back at when your words match one. The look back is a match on words, with no AI call of its own. What it remembers goes to your AI company with your messages. The file is on your computer, and Otian AI cannot see it.

entries.t: Bring in what ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini knows about you
entries.s: Archie gives you one sentence to send ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Paste its answer back, tick the lines to keep, and your agent remembers them.
entries.x: On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Memory, press Bring in what it knows about you. In Archie, the first setup screen also has a card, Bring in what ChatGPT knows. On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Memory, press Bring in what it knows about you. Copy the sentence Archie gives you and send it to ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Paste its answer back and press Show me the lines. Tick the lines to keep and press Remember these. On the owner's phone, Archie Mobile has the same screen under More, then Documents, then Memory, while the computer running Archie is on. Archie never talks to ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. It reads the text you paste, once. About 25 to 30 short facts fit in what it carries. The rest goes to older memory, and the screen shows which before you press. A line with a password, a card number, or a Social Security or account number is never kept. An address or a health detail comes over if you tick it. Kept lines go to your AI company with your messages, as everything in memory does.

entries.t: Send files to your agent, and get files back
entries.s: Send your agent photos, a video, a recording or a document in Archie, and it sends files it made back the same way.
entries.x: In the chat, with the Add button beside the message box, or by dropping files on the conversation. Press Add beside the message box, or drag files onto the conversation. Send the message. For a video or a recording, press Watch it or Listen to it on the card, or Skip. Up to four pictures and one video or recording per message. It asks before it watches a video or listens to a recording, and needs the Video Synthesizer add-on to do either. A document you send is kept under General on the Knowledge tab until you remove it. A recording sent through a chat app such as Telegram is heard as you talking and answered, with no notes made.

entries.t: Your whole agent in one backup file
entries.s: Everything you built goes in one file you save where you like, with no key or token in it. Archie can save one every week.
entries.x: On the Account page, under Backups: Save a backup, Save one every week, and Restore a backup. On the Account page, under Backups, press Save a backup and choose where it goes. For one every week, press Choose a folder under Save one every week. Archie keeps the last three. On another computer, sign in as you and use Restore a backup. It is a plain file holding your chats, lists and documents, so keep it somewhere you would keep a tax return. Keys and passwords stay out. On a new computer you get a list of what to connect again. Downloaded tools, Mac permissions and a paired phone do not travel. Browser sign-ins and a Signal link are dropped on a different computer. It opens only in Archie, on a computer signed in as you.

entries.s: Your agent writes the actual file, such as a PDF, a Word file, a spreadsheet or a deck, and tells you where it put it.
entries.x: Files land in Downloads, in the Archie folder. The switch is on your agent's Setup tab, under What it can do. Ask your agent for a file, for example "Put that in a spreadsheet." Find it in the chat, or in Downloads, inside the Archie folder. It chooses the filename and never the folder. Everything goes to Downloads, in the Archie folder, on the computer running Archie. Eleven kinds only: .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx, .csv, .docx, .md, .txt, .json, .html, .ics and .vcf. It never makes video. One file is 5 MB at most.

entries.s: Ask for a PDF and your agent lays it out on your computer, with headings, bullets, page breaks, and real bar, line or pie charts drawn in.
entries.x: Ask your agent for a PDF, for example "Make me a PDF of this month's expenses with a chart." Charts are bars, a line or a pie, one set of numbers each. A bar chart always starts at zero. A pie leaves out any slice at or below zero. With nothing above zero, it lists the numbers instead. A Word file gets a chart's figures written out instead of the picture.

entries.s: Ask for a deck and you get a real PowerPoint file you can open and change, with each heading starting a slide.
entries.x: Ask your agent for a deck, for example "Turn these notes into a five slide deck." It lands in Downloads, in the Archie folder, and is 5 MB at most.

entries.t: Change a spreadsheet, Word file or deck you give it
entries.s: Give your agent a spreadsheet, Word file, deck or text file and ask for a change. Once you confirm, it sends back a changed copy in the same style.
entries.x: Send the file in the chat, or add it on your agent's Knowledge tab, under Documents. Ask for the change, such as a new expense row or a different sentence. Ask how a total is worked out and it reads the formulas. Press Confirm when it shows you the change. Open the changed copy it sends back. Send the file on any chat app except Signal, which sends and receives no files. It changes Archie's copy. The file where you keep it stays as it was. A total that depends on a changed cell updates when the file is next opened in Excel. Until then your agent reads the old total. A row goes at the end of a list. A slide's lines can change, and it cannot add a slide. A PDF, an .xls or an .ods file is only read. Pages, Numbers, Keynote, an older .doc or .ppt, or a file with macros has to be exported first.

entries.s: Your agent can make a picture and send it to you in the conversation, drawn with OpenAI or Google on your own account.
entries.x: If your AI account is with another company, add a Gemini key for pictures on your agent's Setup tab, under Pictures. Ask your agent for a picture, for example "Draw a logo idea for a lawn care business." If your AI account is not OpenAI or Google, first add a Gemini key on your agent's Setup tab, under Pictures. It sends the picture in your chat app or Archie Mobile, and where a chat app cannot take a file, it saves it on the computer and says where. With only a Claude account and no Gemini key for pictures, it cannot draw. Each picture is billed by the AI company that draws it, never on our credits. What you ask for goes to OpenAI or Google, whichever draws it. No video or music.

entries.s: With no direct connection, your agent can use a website itself in a browser window on your computer: it reads, clicks and types, and you can watch.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Computer control. Switch on Let this agent click and type for you, then add a site. On the Connections tab, open Computer control. Switch on Let this agent click and type for you. Press + Add a website (+ Add a website or app on a Mac) and type the site's address. Sign in yourself in the window that opens, then close it. Ask your agent for the errand in the chat. Tap Press it for me from Archie Mobile or your chat app, and Archie Mobile can switch Computer control, buying, and each site on or off. Signing in to a site happens at your computer. It never types a password, a card you pay with or a sign-in code. Where one is asked for, it stops and hands you the window. Before a press that sends, submits or finalizes something, it sends you the page. Tap Press it for me, or finish it yourself. A purchase needs buying switched on, at a shop you picked, up to a limit you set. Moving money and signing a contract are always yours to press. It is off until you switch it on. Sites under Blocked sites are never opened, and each job stops after the time you set.

entries.s: Send your agent to look around a site before it does anything real there. It clicks through, finishes nothing, and notes how the site is laid out for next time.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Computer control, press Practice beside a site you added. On the Connections tab, open Computer control. Press Practice beside a site you added. Or say yes when your agent offers a practice run. It types only in the search box, stays on that one site, and finishes nothing. A practice run does not make a site safe. Every stop still applies on the real errand afterward. It uses your AI like any other job. It starts only when you press Practice or say yes. Nothing explores on its own.

entries.s: Your agent finds the flight in your confirmation email, checks in on the airline's site the day before, takes a free seat, and sends you the boarding pass.
entries.x: Add Flight Check-In from the Marketplace. It works through Computer control, on the Connections tab. Add Flight Check-In from the Marketplace. Switch on Computer control on the Connections tab. Connect the mailbox your flight confirmations arrive in. It buys nothing: not a seat, a bag or priority boarding. If check-in cannot finish without paying, it stops and tells you what is asked for. It checks in only. It does not book, change or cancel a flight. Where an airline wants an account sign-in or sends a code, it hands you the window.

entries.t: Your agent uses apps on a Mac
entries.s: On a Mac, your agent can use the apps you allow, such as Numbers or Preview, without moving your pointer. If you start using that app, it waits for you.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Computer control, press + Add a website or app and type the app's name. On the Connections tab, open Computer control and switch on Let this agent click and type for you. Press + Add a website or app and type the app's name. When macOS asks, allow Archie in System Settings. The panel's Open System Settings button takes you there. Ask your agent for the job in the chat. Archie Mobile can switch Computer control and each app on or off. The macOS permission is given at the Mac. Mac only. On Windows, Computer control covers websites. It never uses Terminal, password keepers, System Settings, Mail, Messages, Calendar, or your web browsers, whatever you allow. It never types a password or a card you pay with, and anything it could not undo waits for you. An app that does not describe its window cannot be used yet, and one that draws its own boxes may not take typing. Your agent says so and asks you.

entries.s: Ask for somewhere to eat near the office open at eight, and your agent looks it up on the map: name, street, distance, phone number and hours.
entries.x: It uses TomTom, on the Connections tab under Apps, the same connection that works out when to leave for a drive. Connect TomTom on the Connections tab, under Apps. Its key is free and needs no card. Ask your agent for a place near somewhere. Ask the same way from Archie Mobile or a chat app. The map has no ratings or prices, so your agent does not say what is good or cheap. Hours come from the map, which is sometimes out of date. Every reply has the phone number so you can check. Without the TomTom connection your agent does not offer it.

entries.s: Ask Price Watch to check your prices, and your agent looks up what Shopify stores charge right now, whether it is in stock, and a link to that store's checkout.
entries.x: Add Price Watch from the Marketplace. Add Price Watch from the Marketplace. Ask it to check your prices. Amazon, Walmart and the other big marketplaces are not Shopify stores, so for those it searches the web. It only reads. An order is placed on the store's own page, under the Buying switch. A price is what the store showed at that moment.

entries.t: Your agent takes on the jobs you pick
entries.s: Each agent carries only the add-ons you put on it, so it fits the way you work and a reply costs less than carrying every one.
entries.x: In the Marketplace. Open the Marketplace. Add the add-ons for the jobs you want this agent to do. Archie Mobile can add an add-on to an agent or take one off. There is no figure for how much less a reply costs. With nothing added, your agent still answers questions, sets reminders, remembers what you tell it and keeps files. Every add-on is included with Archie, at no extra price.

entries.s: Every skill, routine, specialist and personality in the store comes with Archie, with no price of its own.
entries.x: In the Marketplace. A new computer does not get your add-ons by itself. Restore a backup, or add them again.

entries.t: Written setups for four lines of work
entries.s: Tell Archie you rent portable restrooms or event restroom trailers, run a home trades company, or sell homes, and it starts with that work's lists and a few rules.
entries.x: The rules are on the Personality tab, under Who this agent serves, and the Dashboard card that names the setup opens them. Answer your agent's first questions about what work you do. Change any list or rule by asking your agent. Archie Mobile shows the lists and their counts, and on iPhone opens on the card that names the setup. Only these lines of work and lead generation have written setups. Every other business gets lists drafted from what you tell it. The rules are what your agent is told. You still check what it writes, such as an ad. It does not connect to the software these businesses use. The lists fill from chat, email, your own entries and spreadsheets you bring in. It happens at the first questions, and the match can miss.

entries.t: A written setup for lead generation
entries.s: Tell Archie your business sells leads, calls or booked appointments, and it starts with Clients, Sources and Orders lists and rules about consent and promises to clients.
entries.x: The rules are on the Personality tab, under Who this agent serves. Answer your agent's first questions about what work you do. Only for businesses whose product is leads, calls or appointments. A business buying leads for itself gets no setup. The rules shape what your agent writes. You are still responsible for consent and for what you send.

entries.t: Job Hunt shows where the people you know work
entries.s: Drop in the connections file LinkedIn emails you and Job Hunt shows where the people you know work now, then drafts a note to the right one.
entries.x: With the Job Hunt skill on your agent, drop the file into the chat. Download the connections file LinkedIn emails you. Drop it into the chat, zip and all. Press Add on the card, then See where they work. Ask who you know at a company, and it says who to write to first and drafts the note. You can send the file from Archie Mobile or a chat app as well. It reads a file you drop in and never connects to LinkedIn. A newer file adds new people and leaves the rest as they were. It drafts and never sends. An email draft goes when you press Send, and a LinkedIn note you paste yourself. The file has each person's current employer and title only, and most people have no email address in it. No real LinkedIn export has been brought in yet.

entries.s: An add-on is a text file your agent reads: written instructions plus settings. It brings no code of its own, and nothing in it runs as a program.
entries.x: An add-on can only use tools Archie already has. A new service, tool or screen comes in an Archie update. The one way to give your agent tools Archie never shipped is an app's address for AI assistants, added under Something else on the Connections tab.

entries.t: Ask whether your agent can do something
entries.s: Ask your agent whether it can do something, and it searches the Marketplace's add-ons for one that fits, or offers to write a new skill when none does.
entries.x: In the chat with your agent. Ask in your own words, like "can you keep track of my medications?" Your agent tells you what it found, up to five add-ons. Say yes in your next message to add one, or ask it to write a skill instead. Ask the same way from Archie Mobile or a chat app, then say yes in your next message. It matches words in add-on names and descriptions and reads back up to five, so it can miss the best fit. Nothing is added until you say yes in a later message. It searches the copy of the store Archie had when your agent started. On a shared agent only the owner can add one. Anyone else is told to ask the owner.

entries.t: Write a skill by describing it
entries.s: Say what you wish your agent could do, in your own words. It asks a couple of questions, writes the skill, and shows you a card to keep it.
entries.x: In the chat, or on Build a skill in the agent's sidebar. To fill in the fields yourself, press Build your own on the Skills tab. Tell your agent what you wish it did, like "prep me before a call". Answer its questions. Read the card, which names what it assumed. Press Keep it, or Change something to adjust it. Archie Mobile has a form for writing a skill by hand. A skill you write can only use what Archie can already do: it is instructions plus permission to use existing tools. Skills, routines and specialists can be written this way. Personalities come only from the Marketplace. The form on the Skills tab offers fewer services than the chat does. A skill you write stays on your agent. Getting one into the Marketplace for other people goes through a review we do by hand.

entries.t: Connect a service that is not listed
entries.s: Connect a service Archie does not list, using the web address of its API and your key, then write a skill that tells your agent which addresses to call.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Apps, press Something else at the foot of the list. On the Connections tab, open Apps and press Something else. Give it a name, the web address of its API, and the key that service gave you. Write a skill that uses it, and tell your agent which addresses to call. It works with a service that answers over https and takes a key. A service that will not give you a key cannot be connected this way. Archie knows only the address and the key. You supply the paths in the skill. Reading runs on its own. Anything that changes something waits for your yes, and that cannot be switched off.

entries.s: Add each class's syllabus and your agent tracks the term: what is due this week, what you need on the final, and the school's own deadlines two weeks ahead.
entries.x: Add My Classes and Class Planner from the Marketplace (the College pack has both), then add each syllabus on the agent's Knowledge tab. Add My Classes from the Marketplace. Add each class's syllabus on the Knowledge tab. If you like, paste your class calendar link from your school's site. At registration time, give Class Planner your degree audit. It never turns work in, registers you, or drops a class. It cannot see grades in your school's system, open seats, a waitlist, or a hold on your account. The class calendar link carries only what a professor put a date on. The syllabus is the better source. Reading your school's emails needs a mailbox connected, and the starter credits cannot read mail.

entries.t: What the first run says before connecting
entries.s: On the first run, before you connect a calendar or count your inbox, your agent says what it will read, where that goes, and how to disconnect it later.
entries.x: On the first run, on the Which calendar? and Which email? panels. On the first run, press the calendar or inbox card. Read what your agent says it will read, then pick your account. Connected this way, the calendar is read only. To let your agent change events, press Reconnect on the account's row and check that box. The inbox count asks no AI, but the count then sits in your conversation, which your agent can read back later. The trash can takes the account off your agent. Its sign-in stays under Settings, Saved keys, and Google or Microsoft keeps its permission until you remove it in that account. If the first run connected nothing, it offers Connect my email, Connect my calendar, and Not now once. After Not now, use the Connections tab.

entries.s: When your agent says your calendar, your email, or an app is not connected, a button under its reply opens the Connections tab with the sign-in ready.
entries.x: Under your agent's reply in Chat, such as Connect my calendar or Connect Follow Up Boss. It opens the agent's Connections tab. Press the Connect button under the reply. Pick your account and sign in, in your browser, with the boxes you want checked. Archie Mobile shows a line saying where on the computer to press it, since a phone cannot connect an account. Chat apps get the words only. It shows only under a reply that names the Connections tab, or an unconnected app by its own name. There is no button for a to-do list, since Todoist and Google Tasks are in different places. It opens the screen. Signing in is still yours to do. Chat apps get the words only.

entries.t: Connect an app's address for AI assistants
entries.s: Some apps hand out an address for AI assistants. Add it under Something else, and the tools that app offers join your agent's tools without an Archie update.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Apps, press Something else at the foot of the list. On the Connections tab, open Apps and press Something else. Under What do you call it?, type the app's name. Under Its address, paste the address the app gave you for AI assistants, then paste its key. If the app has you sign in on its own site instead, Archie opens that sign-in in your browser. A tool the app marks as read only runs on its own. Anything else waits for your yes, like every other change. The app has to give you a key or a sign-in. An address that refuses a key cannot be connected. An app that changes its sign-in often may ask you to sign in again after Archie restarts. It has had very little testing with real apps so far.

entries.s: Google, Microsoft, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, Todoist, Fireflies, GoHighLevel, and any service you connect with your own key are reached directly from your computer.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files; Apps; Home devices; and Computer control. Google Drive is per file: your agent sees only the Sheets and Docs you pick in Google's picker. What your agent reads from a connected service goes to your AI company, like anything else it reads. A service you connected yourself is yours. We make no claim about it working.

entries.s: Add Philips Hue, WiZ or LIFX lights from your own wifi, and your agent switches them over that wifi. The request never leaves your network.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Home devices, press Look for devices. On the Connections tab, open Home devices. Press Look for devices. For a Hue bridge, press the round button on top of the bridge when Archie asks. Press Add beside each light you want. To find a Hue bridge, Archie asks Philips once which bridges have reported in from your network. Switching a light stays on your network. What your agent learns from a light, like its name and whether it is on, goes to your AI company like anything else it reads. No locks, thermostats or cameras. The Hue bridge talks to Philips on its own, and Archie has no part in that traffic.

entries.s: Connect iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, AOL, Zoho or GMX mail with an app password you make on the provider's own site, plus its calendar where it has one.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files, choose iCloud or other email. On the Connections tab, open Email, calendar, files. Choose iCloud or other email, then your provider. Make an app password on the provider's site, paste it including spaces, and connect. There is no Sign in with Apple. The app password is the whole connection. The password is kept in your computer's password store and sent only to that provider's own mail and calendar servers. AOL and GMX have no calendar here. For the others, a calendar appears only if Archie found one while connecting. Your agent can do only what connecting proved, such as reading, sending, or the calendar.

entries.s: Your agent thinks with an AI account you connect: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq, xAI, DeepSeek, or Mistral, or another service that works like OpenAI's.
entries.x: On each agent's Setup tab, under AI account. Keys you save are listed in Settings, under Saved keys. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose AI account. Pick an AI company. Paste the key you made on that company's website. The free credits you start with run on Claude, because that is the account we pay for. Changing it restarts your agent, which takes a few seconds. Archie does not promise that every AI company does every job equally well.

entries.t: Ask your agent to switch AI company
entries.s: Ask your agent to use a different AI company, such as "use ChatGPT instead", and it switches, or says where to paste a key if you have none saved.
entries.x: In a chat, ask your agent to use a different AI company. If it has no key for that company, paste one where it tells you. You can ask from Archie Mobile or a chat app, since it is a request in a conversation. It changes only when you ask in a conversation. A routine cannot switch it. The switch restarts your agent, which takes a few seconds. You can turn it off on the agent's Setup tab, under What it can do, with Change which AI answers.

entries.t: A model on your own computer
entries.s: Archie can run your agent on a model on your computer through Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp, after checking that the model can use a tool.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under AI account, in the Another provider panel. Install Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp and download a model. Open your agent's Setup tab, choose AI account, then Another provider. Pick the model Archie found and let Archie check it. Nothing is saved until the model has been handed a tool and used it, and many small models never do. Only where what you type goes changes. Your mail, your calendar, the pages your agent reads, and Archie's update and plan checks still use the internet. It is not the default and not the trial. Archie makes no promise about speed or quality on a model like this.

entries.s: Archie keeps its own estimate of what your agents' AI use has cost, this month and all time, by agent and by AI company.
entries.x: On the Account page, under Spending. Open the Account page and choose Spending. Pick This month or All time. It is an estimate from a price table inside Archie. The exact bill is on your AI company's own billing page. Some AI companies are not in the price table, and the page names them.

entries.t: Response quality, and Use this for every skill
entries.s: Pick Economy, Balanced or Best for your agent's replies, and tick Use this for every skill so its add-ons use that setting too.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under Response quality. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose Response quality. Pick Economy, Balanced or Best. Tick Use this for every skill to make every add-on follow it. Archie Mobile can change an agent's Response quality too, under Response quality in More. Many add-ons pick their own setting, so the setting alone barely changes the bill until the box is ticked. Ticking the box also moves add-ons off the level they chose, and Economy answers were weaker in our tests. Web searches stay on Balanced even with the box ticked.

entries.s: Pick your own model for any of Economy, Balanced and Best from your AI company's list, and it runs in replies, skills and anything on a schedule.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under Response quality, in Choose the models yourself. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose Response quality. Open Choose the models yourself. Pick a model for any setting, or press Put all three back to Archie's choices. Archie Mobile can do the same, under Response quality in More. It needs an AI account of your own. On the free credits or the plan with the AI included there is one model. Another provider runs the one model typed on its card, so there is nothing to pick there. Some AI companies publish no list, so you type the model's name from their website. A model you pick runs without extended thinking unless it is the one Archie would have used.

entries.s: Connect any AI service that works like OpenAI's, such as Venice, by pasting its address, a model name and a key.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under AI account, on the Another provider tile. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose AI account. Pick Another provider. Paste the service's address, a model name and a key, copied from its own website. Venice and services like it are not among the seven named AI companies. Archie says nothing about what that service does with what it receives. Read its own pages for that. It runs the one model you typed, whatever Response quality says.

entries.s: When the free credits or your plan's AI for the month run out, your agent says so once, with the ways to keep going, and keeps what you send.
entries.x: A card under the reply in your agent's chat, with Set up an AI account, See the plans, or Open the Account page, and Lists and Calendar. Press the way you want on the card. Keep typing if you like. Each message gets Saved, and your agent answers it once the AI is back. Archie Mobile shows the same ways, each saying where on the computer to do it, with Lists and Calendar to press. A chat app gets them in words. Only your own messages are kept: the newest 20, each cut at 600 characters, and a photo only as its caption. It picks up within about half an hour of the AI coming back, and only while Archie is open on your computer. A reminder asked for while the AI is out is set only once the AI is back, so it can be late. A chat app gets the ways in words, with no prices and no card.

entries.s: If the AI company has a passing problem, Archie asks it once more. If that fails too, the reply says whether anything was saved or sent, with Try again.
entries.x: Under the reply in your agent's chat. Press Try again to send the same words again. Archie Mobile, Telegram, Slack, and Discord show Try again under the reply. It asks once more, and a second failure reaches you. There is no Try again for a picture, a pin, a message over 2,000 characters, or a turn that already saved something. No button on Signal, iMessage, or Matrix, or in Archie while one of those is the chat app. When the AI runs out, you get the card of ways to keep going instead.

entries.t: Choose what your agent can do
entries.s: Switches decide what your agent offers, such as setting reminders or reading the web; turn one off and each message costs a little less.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under What it can do, in Jobs it does for you and Changes it can make to itself. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose What it can do. Turn off any switch you do not want. Turning a switch off does not remove an add-on. Remove add-ons on the Skills tab. Each row says where the job still gets done with the switch off. Ask for something that is switched off and your agent names the screen that turns it back on. The saving is small and has not been measured.

entries.t: What your agent will never do
entries.s: Your agent is awake only when you write, a routine's time comes, or it checks a mailbox you connected. It cannot run a command or text anyone.
entries.x: The guide What your agent will never do, linked from the first screen of the first run. Archie Mobile shows the Python program under an answer, as Archie does. A chat app gets the answer without it. Each limit is on what it does. None of them makes the AI right, and a wrong draft you send is the realistic harm. It can still search the web, read pages and, with Computer control on, use a browser. Specialists you install can take a job from your agent, but cannot hand it on or start anything themselves. On a Mac its only code is a short Python program it runs inside Archie with no internet. Archie on Windows does not run it yet.

entries.s: If you tell your agent you are thinking about hurting yourself, or someone is putting you in danger, it steps out of character and names where to get help.
entries.x: It applies wherever you talk to your agent, including Archie Mobile and chat apps. In the US it names 988, to call or text. Elsewhere it names your local crisis line, your emergency number, or your doctor. Nobody at Otian AI sees the conversation, and nothing is reported. It is a language model reading text, so it can miss someone who does not say it plainly. It offers no counseling. It stops, says it cannot be the one to help, and names who can.

entries.s: On your own AI account, what you write goes straight from your computer to that AI company, and Otian is not in the middle and keeps no copy.
entries.x: Messages through a chat app such as Telegram cross that company's servers, and messages to Archie Mobile cross ours, locked so we cannot open them. The free credits you start with, and the plan with the AI included, run on our AI account, so while you use them your messages pass through our server on the way to Anthropic. Your AI company still receives what you write, and a web search runs on that company's own search service. Archie still checks your plan and counts add-on installs with our server. Neither carries your conversations. It does not make Archie HIPAA or GDPR compliant, because what you write still goes to a cloud AI company.

entries.t: No analytics, and crash reports you can turn off
entries.s: Archie has no analytics service, and its version check-in and its crash and error reports carry your account ID but never anything you wrote, received, or asked for.
entries.x: In Settings, under Privacy, the Send crash reports switch, with a list of what it sends. Open Settings and choose Privacy. Turn off Send crash reports. Archie Mobile has no analytics, crash reporting or advertising code in it. It is on until you turn it off. Off sends nothing more and deletes anything waiting to be sent. Reports carry your account ID, so they are not anonymous. An error that keeps happening sends its error line, and for an add-on, its name and the tool that failed. Your answer to How did you hear about Archie? is sent only when you press one, and this switch does not cover it.

entries.s: Archie checks for updates with a plain request that carries no version number, nothing identifying your computer, and no account.
entries.x: In Settings, under Updates. GitHub and Cloudflare, which serve the update file, see your computer's internet address and the time of the check.

entries.s: The keys you save for AI companies and services are kept in your computer's built-in password store, where we have no way to read them.
entries.x: In Settings, under Saved keys. A key pasted in Archie Mobile on iPhone travels to your computer locked so we cannot open it, and is stored there the same way. A key goes to its own company with each request, which is how that company knows it is you. While your agent is using a key, Archie holds it in memory.

entries.s: Archie writes down each time a saved key is used and each change to who or what can reach your agents, and shows if any line was changed.
entries.x: In Settings, under Privacy, in Access record. Open Settings and choose Privacy. Read Access record. Checked: nothing edited or removed means the check passed. It holds those actions only. What your agent read, wrote or sent is not in it. It shows a change after the fact. Someone who deletes the record and its note in the password store together leaves nothing to check. It stays on your computer, so we never see it and cannot vouch for it. Only Archie for Teams can export the whole record, with Export the whole record.

entries.t: No list of the add-ons you install
entries.s: Adding an add-on raises its public popularity count by one, and we keep only the running total, never a list of which add-ons are yours.
entries.x: The count request is signed in as you, so it is not anonymous. It is sent whichever AI account you use, and stops only if you block our server. Since we keep no list, a new computer needs your add-ons added again, unless you restore a backup.

entries.t: What Archie Mobile asks for on your phone
entries.s: Archie Mobile uses the camera, your photos, your files and the microphone only when you press to scan, pick, take or record something.
entries.x: This is about Archie Mobile itself, on iPhone and Android. A photo, video, file or recording goes to the computer running Archie, locked so we cannot open it, and your agent shows it to its AI company when it looks. On the talk screen, the microphone listens between turns until you press Done, and stops if you leave the app. Archie Mobile has no analytics or advertising code.

entries.s: Reset Archie erases your agents and your saved keys from your computer, disconnects every phone, and empties the phone mailbox.
entries.x: On the Account page, under Resetting Archie, press Reset Archie. On the Account page, choose Resetting Archie. Press Reset Archie, type reset, and press Erase and restart. It leaves the helper that wakes the computer for routines, and Open Archie at login stays as it was set. Downloaded voice and speech models stay, and so does a choice to turn off error reports. On Windows, the uninstaller's box Also remove my Archie data, agents, and settings is a different thing: it leaves your saved keys behind.

entries.t: How long the phone mailbox keeps things
entries.s: Messages between Archie Mobile and your computer wait in a mailbox on Otian's server. The phone deletes each once read, and your computer clears leftovers a day later.
entries.x: To empty it now, on your agent's Setup tab, under Chat app, press Archie Mobile, then Disconnect every phone. This is how Archie Mobile reaches the computer running Archie. There is no fixed limit in days. The clearing needs your computer on and Archie running. The picture of your agent the phone shows stays until you press Disconnect every phone, reset Archie, or delete your account.

entries.s: Nothing on the network can reach Archie. Only three things listen, on your computer and only while in use: a sign-in, the Google Drive picker, and the Computer control browser.
entries.x: Archie's web tools refuse private and local network addresses. Three things can reach local addresses: lights added on your wifi, an AI model on your computer, and the Computer control browser, which is off until you turn it on. The Computer control browser is fenced only by your Blocked sites list.

entries.t: The plan with the AI included
entries.s: For $59 a month or $599 a year, Archie comes with $25 of Claude usage each month, so you need no AI account of your own.
entries.x: Offered when you choose a plan in Archie, beside the plan where you connect your own AI account. Choose a plan in Archie. Pick the one with the AI included. Your agent will not read your email or your texts on this plan. Both work once you connect an AI account of your own. The $25 refills each paid month and nothing rolls over. When it is used, your agent pauses until next month or until you connect your own AI account. What you write passes through our server on the way to Anthropic. The server records what each request cost, never what it said, and keeps no copy. Free credits you have left end when the plan starts.

entries.t: A 14-day trial on your own AI account
entries.s: When a computer has used its free credits, you can still try Archie for 14 days by connecting an AI account of your own.
entries.x: Archie offers it when the free credits cannot be claimed on your computer. Connect an AI account of your own when Archie offers the 14 days. Archie checks that the key works, then starts the trial. You pay your AI company for what your agent uses during the 14 days. Archie still checks your plan, checks for updates and reads the add-on store during the trial. Your conversations do not pass through us. It is offered only after the free credits are used up on that computer.

entries.s: During a free trial, a strip at the bottom of the window says what Archie costs afterward, and the Account page's Your plan row says the same.
entries.x: The strip at the bottom of the Archie window during a trial, with Get a plan. On the Account page, under Sign-in, the Your plan row, with See plans. Press Get a plan on the strip, or See plans on the Your plan row, to open the plan chooser. The strip and the row never name the plan with the AI included. The chooser behind Get a plan and See plans does. Archie for Teams has no free tier. It is $99 a month or $999 a year, on an AI account of your own. The number of answers left on the free credits is an estimate, since one long document costs as much as many short questions. The free credits may be switched off, so the credits line may not appear.

entries.s: Ask your agent what Archie costs or the cheapest way to keep going, and Archie answers from its own price list without asking the AI.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. Type a short question, such as "What does Archie cost?" Ask from Archie Mobile or a chat app, and the answer arrives like any reply. The question has to be about Archie, the AI, or your plan. "What do we charge for a unit?" goes to your agent as usual. Only your own typed question. A teammate's question goes to the agent. The answer does not name the day a plan's AI comes back. The card does. At about three answers left on the free credits, one line under a reply says so, once until the balance goes up.

entries.t: Add your AI account after buying a plan
entries.s: Buy a plan without the AI in it, and Archie asks for your AI account next, so your first agent starts as soon as it is made.
entries.x: The Add your AI account screen, right after you buy a plan and before Archie opens. Later, it is Settings at the bottom of the left sidebar, then Saved keys. Pick your AI company, or press Show me how for the steps to get a key. Paste the key and press Save and open Archie. Or press Not now, and Archie asks again the next time it opens. It saves an AI account you already have. Show me how walks you through getting one from the AI company. Your agents cannot answer anybody until an AI account is saved. Archie for Teams never includes the AI. Archie Mobile has no checkout, so this happens on the computer only.

entries.t: Free on your own AI account, 20 jobs a day
entries.s: Paste a key from an AI company and Archie opens for free, with every skill and routine, up to 20 jobs a day. A plan takes the limit off.
entries.x: Paste the key when Archie first asks for one, or on your agent's Setup tab, under AI account. Make a key at an AI company such as Anthropic or OpenAI. Paste it into Archie when it asks, or on your agent's Setup tab, under AI account. Archie Mobile is not included; it needs a plan or a free trial that is still running. 20 jobs a day. A job is a reply to you, a routine running, or an email it reacts to, and the count starts again at midnight. Routines and the mail and text watches stop at 15, so the last 5 jobs of the day are yours. Free covers one agent, checked when you add one. A plan runs up to ten. Archie only. Archie for Teams has nothing free.

entries.t: Your plan follows your Otian account
entries.s: A plan lives on your Otian account, so signing in on another computer gets the same plan.
entries.x: Only the plan follows you. Your agents are files on the computer, and a backup file is how they move. Add-ons are added again on a new computer. The free starter credits are counted per computer and do not follow the account.

entries.t: What happens when a plan ends
entries.s: A plan you stop runs to the end of the period you paid for. Nothing on your computer is deleted, and what opens next depends on your edition and key.
entries.x: On the Account page, under Your plan, press Manage plan. Save a backup first, on the Account page, under Backups. On the Account page, under Your plan, press Manage plan to stop it. On Archie with an AI key saved, Archie keeps opening at 20 jobs a day. Without a saved key, it asks for one. Archie for Teams has nothing free, so it asks for a plan. Every agent you made stays and keeps working. Adding one past the free allowance of one agent is refused. Save a backup before you stop. The screen that asks for a plan also has Save a backup of your agents.

entries.t: Move your agents into Archie for Teams
entries.s: When you hire, save a backup in Archie and open it in Archie for Teams, and your agents arrive with their knowledge, lists, routines and memory.
entries.x: In Archie, on the Account page, under Backups. In Archie for Teams, the first run asks Have you used Archie before? with Open a backup. In Archie, open the Account page and choose Backups. Press Save a backup. In Archie for Teams, press Open a backup and pick the file. Reconnect your accounts from the list it shows. Keys and sign-ins do not come across, so you reconnect your accounts once, from a list. It goes one way only. Archie keeps its own copy of each agent, so press Stop on each one there. Opening it replaces the agents already in Archie for Teams, which are kept in a folder and can be put back.

entries.s: A new Archie for Teams agent starts with Team Starter: a shared to-do list, a record of who took which job, web lookups, and a personality naming who it answers.
entries.x: In the Marketplace, Team Starter holds Task Manager, Who's Got This, Researcher, and The Team Assistant. On the first run, Who is on my team? puts "On my team:" in the message box. entries.s: Right-click an agent in Archie to open it, start or stop it, rename it, change how it looks, or delete it.
entries.x: On an agent in the sidebar's list of agents, on the agent you are in, or on its card on the Company page. Right-click an agent. Pick what to do. To delete it, type its name first. In Archie Mobile on iPhone, hold an agent's card on the Agents screen for the same menu, while the computer running Archie is on. A deleted agent cannot be brought back. Deleting an agent leaves its accounts and keys for your other agents.

entries.t: Keeps running with the window closed
entries.s: Close Archie's window and your agent keeps working. Archie stays running in the Dock on a Mac, or by the clock on Windows, until you quit it.
entries.x: On a Mac, click Archie in the Dock or its icon in the menu bar to bring the window back. On Windows, click its icon by the clock. Your agent runs only while Archie is running and your computer is awake. Quitting Archie switches it off. Quitting while an agent is running asks first.

entries.s: Archie opens by itself, with no window, when you sign in to your computer, so your agent is answering again after a restart.
entries.x: Settings, General, Open Archie at login. To turn it off, open Settings, then General, and switch off Open Archie at login. An update turned it on once for everyone, so check the switch if you had turned it off before. Once you switch it off, it stays off.

entries.t: Open Archie with a few keys
entries.s: By default, press Control, Shift and Space on a Mac, or Ctrl, Alt and Space on Windows, and Archie comes forward on your last chat, ready to type.
entries.x: Settings, General, Open Archie from any app. Press the keys in any app while Archie is running. To pick other keys, open Settings, then General, and press Change keys under Open Archie from any app. Switch it off on the same row if you don't want it. It works while Archie is running, including with the window closed, and not after you quit. Your computer tells Archie only when those keys are pressed, and nothing else you type. On a Mac, another app using the same keys may get them first. Nothing happens when you press them? on the row says what to do. It brings Archie's own window forward. There is no small floating box.

entries.t: Archie in the Mac menu bar
entries.s: On a Mac, Archie has an icon in the menu bar at the top of the screen that opens it or quits it.
entries.x: The Archie icon in the Mac menu bar, with Open Archie and Quit Archie. On Windows, the icon by the clock does the same. Click the icon in the menu bar. Choose Open Archie or Quit Archie. There is no switch to hide it. It is there whenever Archie runs on a Mac. Quit Archie asks first while an agent is running.

The buttons under a message sit together in one bar, each in its own color

This is in the Archie window, on an Anthropic account of your own. On the other AI companies, and in Slack, Telegram and the rest, the answer still comes in one piece. Your agent writes a real PDF. Tick Read PDFs that are scans, under Setup, and it looks at the pages instead: up to ten of them, when you ask it to open the file and there was nothing to read.
